title: SpaceX's Starship reaches orbit for the first time, then comes home early
dek: The giant rocket lost an engine on the way up, delivered 26 new Starlink satellites and splashed down after about three hours — a fraction of the flight SpaceX had planned.

body.text: SpaceX put its Starship into orbit around Earth for the first time on Monday, reaching a milestone three years and 13 earlier test flights in the making. The mission was far shorter than planned: controllers brought the vehicle down in the Pacific Ocean north of Hawaii about three hours after it lifted off from the company's Starbase site in South Texas.

Every previous Starship flight had followed a suborbital path, falling back to Earth partway around the planet. On this 14th flight the upper stage reached orbital speed of roughly 17,500 mph, according to [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5983418/spacex-starship-first-orbital-flight-14-nasa) and [the Associated Press](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-supersized-starship-launches-into-orbit-for-the-first-time).
An engine lost on the climb

The flight nearly fell short of orbit. One of the six Raptor engines on the Starship upper stage shut down early during the ascent, and flight controllers had to decide whether to press on. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/spacexs-starship-rocket-reaches-orbit-for-the-first-time/) reported that SpaceX briefly called off the orbital attempt before reversing course minutes later, and [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5983418/spacex-starship-first-orbital-flight-14-nasa) said the decision to continue came about 22 minutes into the flight. With the rest of the vehicle healthy, a later engine burn completed the climb to orbit, [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-on-giant-rockets-first-flight-to-orbit/) reported.

Once there, the ship released 26 of SpaceX's third-generation Starlink internet satellites. [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-on-giant-rockets-first-flight-to-orbit/) described it as the first time the rocket had launched operational satellites, and reported that each new satellite carries ten times the capacity of the generation before it. SpaceX has said a single Starship load of the new satellites adds as much capacity to its network as 20 Falcon 9 launches of the smaller V2 versions, [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/spacexs-starship-rocket-reaches-orbit-for-the-first-time/) reported.

SpaceX had planned six orbits and a splashdown off the coast of Chile. Instead, soon after the satellites were away, it chose to bring the ship down after a couple of laps. The company gave no reason, [the AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-supersized-starship-launches-into-orbit-for-the-first-time) reported. “Flight teams will deorbit Starship safely to our pre-cleared area of the Pacific Ocean after 3 hours in orbit,” SpaceX wrote on X, as quoted by [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/spacexs-starship-rocket-reaches-orbit-for-the-first-time/).

The ship came down tail-first and then tipped over and burst into flames, the usual end for a Starship ocean landing, according to [the AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-supersized-starship-launches-into-orbit-for-the-first-time) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-on-giant-rockets-first-flight-to-orbit/). The Super Heavy booster, which separated about two and a half minutes after liftoff, made a simulated landing in the Gulf of Mexico rather than returning to the tower at its launch site.

Starship is central to NASA's plan to return astronauts to the Moon. A lander version of the vehicle is one of two the agency is paying for, alongside a design from Jeff Bezos's Blue Origin. NASA's Artemis III mission next year is set to practise docking an Orion crew capsule with both landers in Earth orbit, and the first crewed landing, Artemis IV, is targeted for no earlier than 2028. Getting a lander to the Moon will require SpaceX to refuel it in orbit with a series of Starship tanker flights — up to 15 or so, [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-on-giant-rockets-first-flight-to-orbit/) reported.
Managing every step in a safe, responsible and especially inspirational way.
body.attribution: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, congratulating SpaceX, as reported by [the AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-supersized-starship-launches-into-orbit-for-the-first-time) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-on-giant-rockets-first-flight-to-orbit/)

body.text: The company went public in June, and [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5983418/spacex-starship-first-orbital-flight-14-nasa) reported that its filings ahead of the listing warned that any failure or delay in developing Starship would limit its ability to carry out its growth strategy. SpaceX shares rose more than 1% in early trading on Monday but turned negative after the flight was cut short, [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/spacexs-starship-rocket-reaches-orbit-for-the-first-time/) reported.

Starship was designed to be fully reusable, but SpaceX has so far brought its ships down at sea rather than try to catch one at the launch site. The next flight could attempt that catch with the launch tower's mechanical arms, [the AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-supersized-starship-launches-into-orbit-for-the-first-time) reported, and Elon Musk has put the odds of success at even or slightly better. Musk has said the company is being cautious because a ship breaking apart over land could rain debris on people.

SpaceX is also widening where Starship can fly from, with launch sites under construction in Florida, including at Kennedy Space Center, and a planned launch complex in Louisiana that [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5983418/spacex-starship-first-orbital-flight-14-nasa) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/spacexs-starship-rocket-reaches-orbit-for-the-first-time/) both put at roughly $100 billion.
